hint: Watch for “the” versus “a” in the English.

corpus.lang: Rlaavuu quuqanga tiiq kiiqitkaapuu vanaaqnaanganuu kijaqaa.
corpus.en: Sleepy giants did not steal the hens again.

corpus.lang: Rlaavuu vaqapaanaanga tiiq kiilipapuu vaquuqanganuu kijaqaa.
corpus.en: The sleepy sheepdogs did not wake the giants again.

accepted: a hen did not wake the sleepy sheepdogs
toEnglish.explanation: S V O order. naaqnaa = hen; tiiq = NEG; kii-lipa = PST-wake; rlaavuu = sleepy; va-qapaanaa-nga-nuu = DEF-sheepdog-PL-ACC.

toLang.prompt: Sleepy hens do not wake a giant again.
accepted: rlaavuu naaqnaanga tiiq lipapuu quuqanuu kijaqaa
toLang.explanation: S V O order. rlaavuu = sleepy; naaqnaa-nga = hen-PL; tiiq = NEG; lipa-puu = wake-3PL; quuqa-nuu = giant-ACC; kijaqaa = again.

grammar: Word order: subject, verb, object. With one participant: subject, verb.
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
Past tense. Without it the verb is present or future.
On the verb when the subject is plural.
Negation: a separate word before the verb.
Come before the noun. Noun endings go on the noun only; the adjective stays bare.
Go at the end of the sentence.
explain.notes: Checked against 2348 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 2333, including: -nga appears when: definite; -nga appears when: plural & definite.
